title: Boosters and Stance in Academic Writing
text:
Academic writers do not only soften their claims; they also strengthen them when the evidence is compelling. Boosters such as 'clearly', 'undoubtedly', and 'demonstrate' signal the writer's confidence in a finding. Such expressions can persuade readers, but they also carry a risk. A booster that is not supported by data invites skepticism rather than trust.

The choice between a booster and a hedge is therefore a rhetorical decision as much as a scientific one. Reviewers often scrutinize strong claims more closely than cautious ones. Consequently, an experienced author may prefer 'suggests' over 'proves' when the data are incomplete. Their stance, in other words, is calibrated to the reliability of the evidence.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what risk do boosters carry?
options: They invite skepticism when they are not supported by data
They make readers stop reading the article
They are banned by most academic journals
They always lower the writer's credibility

questions.text: What do reviewers often do, according to the second paragraph?
options: Scrutinize strong claims more closely than cautious ones
Reject every paper that contains hedges
Prefer boosters to hedges in all cases

questions.text: What does the passage imply about 'suggests' compared with 'proves'?
options: It signals a weaker, more cautious claim suited to incomplete data
It signals a stronger claim backed by complete data
It is a booster used only in concluding sentences
It has no effect on how readers interpret the claim

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of stance?
options: Stance should match how reliable the evidence is
Stance should always be as confident as possible
Stance is irrelevant once the data are published
Stance matters only in the title of a paper

vocabulary.definition: words that strengthen a claim and show the writer's confidence
so strong or persuasive that it demands attention or belief
to look at something very carefully and critically
adjusted carefully so that it matches a particular standard

paragraph_translations: Autores acadêmicos não apenas suavizam suas afirmações; eles também as reforçam quando as evidências são convincentes. Reforçadores como 'clearly', 'undoubtedly' e 'demonstrate' sinalizam a confiança do autor em um resultado. Tais expressões podem persuadir os leitores, mas também carregam um risco. Um reforçador que não é sustentado por dados provoca ceticismo, em vez de confiança.

A escolha entre um reforçador e uma ressalva é, portanto, uma decisão retórica tanto quanto científica. Pareceristas costumam examinar afirmações fortes com mais atenção do que afirmações cautelosas. Consequentemente, um autor experiente pode preferir 'suggests' a 'proves' quando os dados são incompletos. Sua posição, em outras palavras, é ajustada à confiabilidade das evidências.
